inputs.text: They’re using Harry Wait’s convictions to bury the part that matters: he showed how the registration system could be exploited. He requested ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without consent, and the jury convicted him of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge while acquitting him of another identity theft count. That split verdict gives institutions just enough cover to declare the matter settled and brand scrutiny “false election claims.” The message is clear: punish the person who probes the machinery, then let those invested in keeping it unquestioned decide what the public is allowed to ask.
